title: Contract option matrix & dataflow mapping - residency pricing experiment
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Design and validate a matrix of contract and technical options that map residency commitments to retention tiers and subprocessor controls. The goal is to quantify commercial appetite and engineering cost for standardized residency packaging (EU/UK commitments, VPC options, KMS ownership) and produce legal language and diagrams to accelerate negotiations.
hypothesis: Providing a simple, clearly priced set of residency + retention contract options with explicit subprocessor attestations reduces negotiation friction and increases conversion/willingness-to-pay for regulated customers by >=15% while keeping engineering uplift under target margins.
success_metrics: 30% faster legal review turnaround for pilot deals
<=10% of pilot deals require bespoke engineering beyond listed options
experiment_plan: Draft a 3x3 option matrix: Residency (Global / EU-only / Customer VPC) x Retention (30d / 90d / Custom).
Create dataflow diagrams for each cell showing data location, subprocessors, and key management ownership.
Work with Legal to draft SCC supplement, sample contract clauses, and a standard subprocessor attestation template.
Run a 6-customer sales pilot across fintech, healthcare, and marketplaces; collect redlines and willingness-to-pay signals.
Prepare an enterprise security questionnaire bundle and canonical answers to reduce back-and-forth.
Estimate engineering effort for each matrix cell (audit logs, retention enforcement, VPC onboarding) and capture as ENG work items.
acceptance_criteria: Matrix doc reviewed and signed off by Legal and Security
Dataflow diagrams validated by Engineering and labeled with implementation risk
SCC supplement and subprocessor attestation templates completed
Pilot executed with at least 4 qualified prospects and results documented
